items.loc: Pozuelo de Alarcón, Community of Madrid, Spain
items.desc: Project description Machine learning (ML), including reinforcement learning and supervised learning, has shown significant potential for a wide range of synthesis tasks, including controller synthesis and program synthesis. A promising line of work has combined ML with traditional formal verification in a CEGIS-style loop: ML is used to efficiently explore the space of candidate solutions, while formal verification checks their correctness and provides counterexamples to guide further learning. This demonstrates how ML and formal methods can complement each other in a tightly integrated […] ork, combining the flexibility and scalability of learning with the rigorous guarantees of formal verification. Applications are invited to apply for one phd position at the IMDEA Software Institute, Madrid, Spain. However, existing learning-enabled synthesis frameworks have largely been developed independently for specific domains, resulting in a fragmented landscape of domain-specific techniques. This project aims to take a step towards a more general approach based on Skolem function synthesis, which provides a general formulation of synthesis problems and can encompass problems beyond the domains traditionally considered, including applications such as solving partial differential equations. The goal of this PhD position is therefore to develop a learning-enabled CEGIS framework for Skolem function synthesis, and to use this general framework to address synthesis problems across a range of different domains. The PhD student will be jointly supervised by Kaushik Mallik and Alessio Mansutti. Eligibility Candidates with master’s degrees in CS are welcome to apply. Prior backgrounds in formal verification and/or machine learning will be appreciated but not necessary.  Your investigation will focus on mechanisms that enable Large Language Models (LLMs) and other foundation models to leverage external knowledge representations such as knowledge graphs, ontologies, and formal design representations while preserving the reasoning capabilities of symbolic systems.

items.desc:
How to avoid learning too much - safe and efficient learning for control 
 Job description 
Inefficient operation of industrial systems, electricity production, and heating systems in buildings is currently responsible for over 50% of overall greenhouse gases emissions. Improving energy efficiency of energy-intensive sectors by implementing advanced control systems has the potential to both improve efficiency and reduce the costs, all while continuing to meet safety requirements. The flexibility of safe and adaptive learning control methods makes them crucial for safety-critical applications. […] requirements. The flexibility of safe and adaptive learning control methods makes them crucial for safety-critical applications. A key difficulty in these learning-based approaches lies in the fact that the algorithm must simultaneously learn the model and guarantee safety. This dual requirement significantly impacts the computational cost of the learning algorithm, particularly in situations where the optimal decision evolves over time. We now aim to develop computationally efficient safe learning methods for time-varying optimal control problems.
Existing safe learning algorithms usually assume that they have unlimited access to the experiments and thus unlimited new data. Approaches using limited data sets have been restricted to Bayesian optimization without safety constraints. Moreover, the algorithms typically rely on the repetitive nature of the experiments, for instance in robotics or precision manufacturing. The unlimited data combined with repetitiveness limit the applicability of safe learning algorithms in problems evolving over time, such as residential buildings. This PhD project will explore the connection between the dynamics of the optimized system with numerical properties of optimization algorithms to provide a framework for safe learning with minimal interactions over time. items.title: Doktorand inom Organisatoriska implikationer av artificiell intelligens
items.desc: Projektbeskrivning Forskarutbildningsämne: Industriell ekonomi och organisation Införandet av artificiell intelligens (AI) har spridit sig snabbt inom både offentlig och privat sektor. AI-tekniker – särskilt algoritmer för maskininlärning och stora språkmodeller – blir alltmer centrala. Denna utveckling har gett upphov till AI-ekosystem som sammanför nystartade AI-företag, konsulter och etablerade organisationer, vilket förändrar hur anställda, företag och hela branscher fungerar. Även om vissa tillämpningar ger effektivitetsvinster, ställs organisationer ofta inför kritiska utmaningar, såsom […] låg ekonomisk avkastning, osäkerhet kring kvalitet och svåra etiska dilemman. Detta doktorandprojekt syftar till att kritiskt analysera de organisatoriska konsekvenserna av AI. Doktoranden kan exempelvis utforska frågor som: Hur hanterar organisationer de ledningsmässiga utmaningar som uppstår till följd av AI-teknikers probabilistiska natur? Hur kommer AI att förändra det moderna näringslivet, och vilka möjligheter och risker är förknippade med en sådan omvandling? Vilken roll spelar nystartade företag och konsulter – vid sidan av stora AI-företag – i en ansvarsfull omställning mot en AI-baserad ekonomi? Doktorandtjänsten är en del av Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program – Humanity and Society (WASP-HS), ett nationellt forskningsprogram i Sverige. WASP-HS främjar ny, tvärvetenskaplig kunskap om AI och autonoma system samt deras inverkan på människa och samhälle. Programmet möjliggör forskning i framkant, expertisutveckling och kapacitetsuppbyggnad inom samhällsvetenskap och humaniora. För mer information se här Handledning: Emrah Karakaya föreslås som huvudhandledare, Mats Engwall som biträdande handledare. Beslut fattas vid antagningen. items.title: PhD Position – Lyme Neuroborreliosis in Children: From Understanding Pathogenesis to Precise Diagnosis and Treatment
items.dept: Division of Infectious Diseases and Hospital Epidemiology, University Children's Hospital Zurich
items.desc:
Your main task will be to manage the prospective clinical study of LD in children (BRILLIANT study) in order to draw conclusions on patho-mechanisms of LD and identify new microbiological and immunological markers of Bb infection. Management of the BRILLIANT study: overseeing patient recruitment, scheduling follow-ups, sample processing and storage, extracting data from hospital records, managing study database (REDCap)
 Establishment of Bb cultures from clinical isolates: Further protocol optimization by improving qPCR screening procedure and culture conditions. Evaluation of usefulness of culture and qPCR for clinical diagnosis
 Phenotype the immune response in LD and LNB: Analyze preliminary data, design experiments to further investigate relevant immune cell subsets using flow cytometry, bead-based cytokine/chemokine assay or scRNA-seq approaches
 Identify genotypes of Bb clinical isolates: Perform WGS on new Bb clinical isolates and identify genotypes and virulence factors associated with LD and LNB clinical subgroups
Furthermore, your duties as part of the employment will include: Writing scientific manuscripts (in English)
 Presentation of results at internal meetings and training events
 Participation in national and international conferences (including presenting your work)
 If applicable, supervising Master's students in Biomedicine and Pharmacy
 Master's degree (MSc) in medicine, biology, immunology, or a related field
 Strong interest in clinical research, experience in clinical research is a plus
 Research interest in immunology, microbiology and/or infectious diseases
 Good understanding of statistics, experience with R is a plus
 High motivation, ability to work independenty, good written and oral communication skills
 Good knowledge of German and English
 February 2027 or upon agreement; temporary position for 3 years
